```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

svysem follows the design-based procedure in Oberski (2014, <doi:10.18637/jss.v057.i01>): a lavaan model, and a variance that uses the survey design. No code is taken from lavaan.survey. The agreements that the package tests are with `survey`, with stored lavaan.survey results, and with replicate weights from the same design. Agreement with Mplus output has not been checked. In particular, the weight matrix Mplus uses for `TYPE = COMPLEX` with WLSMV has not been compared with lavaan's diagonally weighted least squares matrix.

```{r setup}
library(svysem)
design <- simulate_design(n_psu = 6, n_per = 5, n_strata = 2, seed = 4)
model <- "f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4"
fit <- svycfa(model, design)
weighted <- lavaan::cfa(model, data = design$variables, sampling.weights = "w")
max(abs(coef(fit) - lavaan::coef(weighted)[names(coef(fit))]))
```

The coefficients above agree because both fits use the sampling weights. The standard errors do not. lavaan treats the rows as independent. svysem also uses the strata and the primary sampling units.

lavaan rescales the sampling weights so that they sum to the number of rows. Means and maximum-likelihood covariances are unchanged by that rescaling, so the same rows are passed to the design with their original weights.

`survey.lonely.psu` is read when the design has a stratum with one primary sampling unit. The fit does not change that option.

MLR fits one group. Single-group MLM is a linearization. With `group=`, MLM uses replicate weights: lavaan keeps one covariance matrix of sample statistics per group, and that matrix drops the covariance between groups. The omission is large enough to move a between-group contrast when primary sampling units contain both groups, so the replicate standard errors are the ones returned. The multigroup MLM chi-square remains the maximum-likelihood statistic. WLSMV accepts `group=` and still passes one matrix per group. Clustering belongs in the design. Passing `cluster=` would count the primary sampling units twice, and svysem rejects it.

MLM uses a Satorra-Bentler adjustment for complete continuous data. MLR uses a Yuan-Bentler adjustment (Yuan and Bentler 2000, <doi:10.1111/0081-1750.00078>), including when `missing = "ml"`. The MLR variance is a sandwich: lavaan's observed information, and the design variance of the casewise scores. WLSMV standard errors are the replicate-weight variance of lavaan's own sample statistics.

For a multiply imputed design, each imputation is fitted and the parameters are pooled with Rubin's rules. The within-imputation variances are the design-based ones. When the imputation model and the analysis design do not match, that pooled variance can be wrong. Kott (1995) describes this for weighted survey data, and Kim, Brick, Fuller and Kalton (2006, <doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2006.00546.x>) show that the bias can be large for a domain mean when many values are imputed. svysem does not correct for it.
